acceptance: pr-hold decides from the pull request's live labels (read through the API), not the event payload, so a rerun of a hold-era suite passes once the label is gone
Or, if the payload stays authoritative: pr-arm recognises a superseded pr-hold failure and names the working remedy instead of make pr-rerun
A test covers this sequence: push while held, remove the label, then rerun the old suite or arm
No change to required contexts or rulesets; the hold still blocks while the label is present
context: Related but distinct: pr-arm-rerun-contradictory-guidance-20261027 covers pr-arm/pr-rerun advice while a full CI run is still in progress.
description:
Problem (2026-11-06, PR #3957 head 47049d6e59): .github/workflows/pr-hold.yml computes HELD from github.event.pull_request.labels, the payload of the triggering event. A push made while no-auto-merge was set produced a failed 'hold' suite. Removing the label produced a newer, successful 'unlabeled' run. make pr-arm then refused: the failure is 'hidden behind a newer success; the merge rollup still counts it, so run make pr-rerun'. make pr-rerun reran it, but a rerun replays the original payload, which still carries the label, so it failed again, and pr-arm refused with 'required check hold completed with conclusion failure'. Only a new head cleared it; here that was a rebase onto develop. Every owner-released hold set before the last push hits this loop.

Outcome: after the owner removes the label, the current head can be armed without pushing a new commit.
